summary_of_pdf: This document is an RMail secure file share download receipt serving as evidentiary proof that Todd Hartman of Best Buy received and downloaded a formal notice of proprietary rights and actual knowledge of pending patent claims under 35 U.S.C. § 154(d). The downloaded files include an SEC Tips, Complaints, and Referrals (TCR) submission, a portfolio of USPTO patent applications, an EPO defensive publication referencing USPTO App. No. 19/640,945, and a Department of Defense license grant involving Heidi Shyu.
attorneys_comments: From an evidentiary standpoint, this RMail receipt is highly probative for establishing 'actual notice' under 35 U.S.C. § 154(d), which is a strict statutory prerequisite for obtaining reasonable royalty damages for pre-issuance patent infringement. The timestamped download logs (April 13, 2026) defeat any plausible deniability by the recipient regarding the receipt of the patent portfolio and associated claims. The inclusion of an SEC TCR suggests parallel securities implications, potentially triggering material risk disclosure duties for the target entity. Furthermore, the DoD license grant indicates potential 28 U.S.C. § 1498(a) implications or DFARS data rights complexities. Procedurally, this document should be authenticated and preserved under Fed. R. Evid. 901(b)(9) as a system record establishing definitive receipt and knowledge.

Monitor the referenced USPTO applications (e.g., 19/640,945) for publication and allowance to perfect the 35 U.S.C. § 154(d) provisional rights. 3.
